title: Chest pain
candidateBrief: You are a junior doctor in the Emergency Department. David Evans, 58, has presented with chest pain that started 90 minutes ago. Take a focused history. You may use the Examine and Investigations panels. You will be asked questions afterwards.

patient.name: David Evans
patient.setting: Emergency Department cubicle, on a trolley.
patient.openingStatement: I've got this awful pain in my chest, doctor. It came on while I was carrying the shopping in.
patient.demeanour: Clammy, uncomfortable, rubbing his chest, frightened but trying to stay calm. Speaks in slightly short bursts.
patient.speechStyle: Plain everyday language, describes the pain as 'like an elephant sitting on me'. No medical terms.

ice.ideas: Hopes it's indigestion from a big breakfast.
ice.concerns: His dad died of a heart attack at 60 and he is scared the same is happening.
ice.expectations: Wants something for the pain and to know what's going on.

freelyShared: The pain started 90 minutes ago while carrying heavy shopping and hasn't gone away.
It is in the centre of his chest and feels heavy and tight.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: whether the pain goes anywhere else
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: It goes into my left arm and up into my jaw.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: sweating, nausea, breathlessness, palpitations or dizziness
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I've been sweating buckets and I feel a bit sick. Bit short of breath too.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: how bad the pain is or a score out of ten
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: It's an eight out of ten. Worst pain I've ever had.
For a few weeks I've had a tightness walking up hills, but it went off after a couple of minutes' rest.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: smoking, blood pressure, cholesterol or diabetes
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I smoke about 20 a day. I was told my blood pressure was high a while back but never went back for tablets. Not diabetic as far as I know.
My dad died of a heart attack when he was 60.
I don't take anything regularly. No allergies.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: pain on breathing or moving, tearing pain to the back, recent travel or leg swelling
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: It doesn't change when I breathe or move, it's not tearing, and it doesn't go to my back. No long trips, legs are fine.

patient.cue: It's just not easing off, doctor. Is it my heart?

examFindings.finding: HR 96 regular, BP 158/94 in both arms, RR 20, SpO2 96% on air, temperature 36.8°C.
Heart sounds normal, no murmurs. JVP not raised. Peripheral pulses equal.

investigations.result: 2 mm ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL.
Normal heart size, clear lung fields, normal mediastinum.

postEncounterQuestions.q: What is the most likely diagnosis?

postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Call for senior help and activate the primary PCI pathway; aspirin loading dose, analgesia (e.g. IV morphine with antiemetic), oxygen only if hypoxic, GTN if not hypotensive, continuous monitoring, IV access and bloods, second antiplatelet as per local protocol.

items.text: Takes a structured pain history (site, onset, character, radiation, severity, timing, exacerbating/relieving)
items.evidenceHint: where, when, what does it feel like, go anywhere, score

items.text: Asks about associated symptoms (sweating, nausea, breathlessness)
Asks questions to exclude important differentials (PE, dissection, pericarditis)
Acknowledges his fear and explains what happens next honestly
